title: ai_governance_redline_checklist
primary_keyword: what AI cannot do in marketing
claim: Enterprise AI adoption fails in governed industries because teams deploy tools before defining non-negotiable redlines for regulatory and brand protection.
hook: Deploying AI without redlines is a liability.

evidence.detail: A 3-part operational boundary test for evaluating LLM deployment in regulated B2B marketing workflows: regulatory claim verification, liability assignment, and technical parameter verification.

reel_script.onscreen: Deploying AI without redlines is a liability.
reel_script.voiceover: Deploying AI without redlines is a liability. Most B2B marketing teams focus on tool speed, but legal and compliance focus on exposed risk.
Understanding what AI cannot do in marketing starts with defining hard operational boundaries before software reaches your team.
First, demand explicit evidence. Every factual claim, performance metric, or compliance specification requires mandatory human review before publication.

items.label: Fact check gate
items.detail: Require named source for every claim

reel_script.voiceover: Second, assign accountability. If output violates regulatory standards or commercial terms, an internal owner must hold explicit approval signoff.

items.label: Audit logging
items.detail: Retain prompts and edits for compliance

reel_script.voiceover: Third, verify data isolation. Ensure customer data and proprietary engineering files are never used to train external foundation models.

items.label: Model isolation
items.detail: Zero data retention on vendor servers

items.label: IP protection
items.detail: Block public LLM scrapers on assets

reel_script.voiceover: AI governance is an operating boundary, not a software feature.

caption:
Deploying AI without redlines is a liability.

When evaluating what AI cannot do in marketing, large industrial organisations rarely fail due to technology limits. They fail because comms and legal teams argue over output after it reaches executive review.

Generative tools accelerate text generation, but they do not assume legal liability for unverified claims, regulatory non-compliance, or leaked operational data.

If your marketing tech stack allows unvalidated technical claims to move directly from an LLM prompt to a customer document, your governance is broken.

True integration requires hard boundaries: mandatory source verification, named human accountability for regulatory claims, and strict data isolation guarantees.

Governance is an operating boundary, not a software feature.

Send this to whoever is setting your marketing technology guardrails this quarter.
